title: Rust: While Loop
description: Use while loops to repeat code in Rust.

steps.title: Count Down
steps.description: Start with `count = 5` and use a while loop to print each value down to 0.
hints: Don't forget to decrement `count` inside the loop!
Without decrementing, the loop runs forever.

verification.failureMessage: Print numbers from 5 down to 0 using a while loop.

steps.title: Sum of Numbers
steps.description: Use a while loop to calculate the sum of numbers from 1 to 10. Print the result.

verification.failureMessage: Print the sum of 1 to 10 (should be 55).

steps.title: Loop Until Condition
steps.description: Start with `x = 1`. Double x until it exceeds 100 using a while loop. Print each value of x.

verification.failureMessage: Print values as x doubles from 1 until exceeding 100.

steps.title: Nested While Loops
steps.description: Use nested while loops to print a 3x3 grid of coordinates like `(0,0) (0,1) ...`
hints: Outer loop for rows (i), inner loop for columns (j).

verification.failureMessage: Print all 9 coordinate pairs from (0,0) to (2,2).

steps.title: Loop with break
steps.description: Use `loop { }` (Rust's infinite loop) with a `break` statement. Start at `1`, count up, and break when you reach `10`. Print each value.
hints: `loop { println!("{}", i); if i >= 10 { break; } i += 1; }`
`loop` is Rust's keyword for infinite loops.
Use `break` to exit the loop when a condition is met.

verification.failureMessage: Print numbers 1 to 10 using loop with break.
